page.layout: One column of running text, centred on the printed page, with the running head above it and the page number at the top right. A blank margin is at the left. Bleed-through from the facing page appears at the left edge and is not transcribed. The catchword sits at the lower right below the last line.

p.i: Tes naturale desiderium suavium rerum, sed an-equam natura expetat eas, imples atq; obruis te-dis, priusquam esuris: bibis antequam sitis: con-vimenta varia ad irritandum famem excogitas: ina praeciosa, ut inuites sitim coparas. Et ut sua-iter dormias, non modo mollia strata, sed etiam ectos facis. Somnium enim accersis, non ut per la-boris interualla quiescas, sed inopia negocij: sine udore ac legum metu, amori, operam das: nocte buteris, & optimam diei partem somno perdis. t cum deam te esse glorieris, ex deorum nume-o eiecta es. Asspernantur te & honesti homines, eq; unquam suauissimum carmen tuas laudes ce-brans audiuisti: & pulcherrimum spectaculum unquam uidisti. Nullum enim unquam recte fa-ctum tuum spectasti. Quis tibi improba credet? uis egenti dabit aliquid? quis sanae mentis in tuo choro esse uelit? Vbi iuuenes imbecilli corpore unt, senes fatui, qui cum adolescentiam in otio perdiderint, senectutem miseram & calamito-am agunt, tunc & pudet ante actae vitae, & piget rimum quaerere necessaria aetati subsidia: suauia adolescentia ante tempus praecerpserunt, labo-rem & aerumnas in aetatem eam distulerunt. Ego vero apud deos uersor, & apud honestos homi-es: nullum honestum facinus neq; dij, neq; ho-ines sine me faciunt, Ideoq; me & dij & homi-nes

page.notes: The first letters of several lines are cut off or covered by bleed-through from the facing page at the left edge, so the opening fragments (such as "Tes", "eq;", "uis", "choro") are read from the visible remnants and may be incomplete. The first line probably begins with a cut-off letter before "tes". The long s is transcribed as s throughout. The catchword "nes" is the opening of the next page, placed at the lower right. The "&" signs are the printed Et ligature. Words at line ends are hyphenated as printed.
